settings.tagline: Care Family Home. Touching Lives. Connecting Families to What They Need.
settings.heroHeadline: A Care Family Home That Connects Everyone to Hope.
settings.heroSubheadline: HIS AND HERS is a vibrant community-based organization rooted in prayer, mental wellbeing, safe refuge, children’s home partnerships, rehabilitation support, and autism family care—uniting individuals, families, and organisations to touch lives together.
settings.welcomeHeadline: Where Individuals, Families & Partner Organisations Build Stronger Homes
settings.welcomeBody: Like a true care family home, HIS AND HERS connects people directly to what they need: corporate and group visits to verified children’s homes, mental health counselling to lighten heavy burdens, nearby rehabilitation centres for families in recovery, safe refuge from abuse, and practical ASD guidance for parents and kids.
settings.prayerInvitation: Whatever season your family or heart is walking through, you do not have to navigate it alone. We are here to listen, connect you to real care, and stand beside you.
settings.closingStatement: At HIS AND HERS, we are a care family home where every child is seen, every burden is shared, and families find clear pathways to healing.

asdGuides.title: Creating a Calm Sensory Corner at Home
asdGuides.summary: Autistic children often experience lights, loud echoes, and clutter more intensely. A predictable low-stimulation corner helps their nervous system reset gently.
practicalSteps: Choose a quiet corner with soft natural light or warm lamp lighting instead of harsh overhead bulbs.
Keep a familiar basket of comforting textures (weighted blanket, soft cushion, fidget toy, or noise-cancelling ear defenders).
Never use the calm corner as punishment—introduce it when your child is happy so it feels like a safe harbour.

asdGuides.title: Understanding Meltdowns vs. Tantrums With Love
asdGuides.summary: A meltdown is sensory or emotional overload—not bad behaviour. Lowering demands and staying calm helps your child feel safe faster.
practicalSteps: Speak softly using short, calm sentences (or pause talking altogether while ensuring physical safety).
Reduce triggers right away: dim bright lights, turn off loud TVs, and give breathing space without lecturing.
Wait until after your child is fully settled to reconnect with water, a hug (if welcomed), or a gentle visual check-in.

asdGuides.title: Using Picture Schedules & Gentle Transitions
asdGuides.summary: Knowing what happens next reduces anxiety. Simple visual cards and 5-minute countdown warnings make mornings, meals, and bedtime smoother.
practicalSteps: Place 4–5 simple picture or drawn cards in order for key routines (Wake Up → Brush Teeth → Breakfast → School).
Give clear countdown warnings before stopping play (“5 more minutes with blocks, then bath time”).
Celebrate all communication—speech, pointing, picture exchange, gestures, or typing are all valid voices.

asdGuides.title: Helping Siblings, Relatives & Communities Understand
asdGuides.summary: Extended family and community spaces thrive when people learn patience, clear sensory kindness, and joy in every child’s unique strengths.
practicalSteps: Explain autism to siblings simply: “Their brain notices sounds and feelings extra strongly, so quiet kindness helps them shine.”
Share a short one-page “How I Like to Be Greeted” note with teachers, Sunday caregivers, and relatives.
Build around your child’s special interests (trains, music, drawing, patterns)—they are wonderful bridges to joy and learning.

impactProjects.title: Children’s Home Mentorship & Care Hamper Day
impactProjects.summary: Corporate volunteers and community friends partnered together to spend a joyful day reading, playing, and equipping a partner children’s home.
impactProjects.whatWasDone: HIS AND HERS coordinated a vetted corporate CSR team and local storytellers to bring reading books, school packs, fresh produce, and unhurried mentorship games to a partner children’s home.
impactProjects.whyItMattered: Children thrive on genuine presence and long-term care, not drop-off charity. Structured visits ensure safeguarding, warmth, and real friendship.
impactProjects.whoItServed: 42 children aged 3–16 alongside house mothers and dedicated residential caregivers.
impactProjects.whatGlowHopedToAchieve: To connect caring organisations and everyday individuals directly with verified children’s homes.
impactProjects.documentedStory: Under wide courtyard trees, teams read stories side by side, shared fruit and lunch, and pledged ongoing termly stationery support.
impactProjects.imageAlt: Corporate volunteers and community members reading with children at a partner children home

impactProjects.title: Youth Encouragement & Mental Wellbeing Circles
impactProjects.summary: Intergenerational mentorship and listening tables creating safe spaces for young people to speak openly, receive guidance, and lighten emotional burdens.
impactProjects.whatWasDone: We hosted welcoming afternoon sessions pairing trained community mentors, counsellors, and educators with youth for open dialogue and emotional wellbeing conversations.
impactProjects.whyItMattered: Many young people carry quiet pressures around mental health, family stress, and belonging. Having trusted adults who listen breaks isolation.
impactProjects.whoItServed: Teenagers, students, and young adults from across diverse neighbourhoods.
impactProjects.whatGlowHopedToAchieve: To cultivate a supportive environment where young people feel heard, safe, and connected to caring mentors and counsellors.
impactProjects.documentedStory: Seated around long wooden tables with notebooks and tea, mentors and students reflected on emotional resilience, hope, and community care.
impactProjects.imageAlt: Community mentors and youth seated together around wooden tables in warm conversation

impactProjects.title: ASD Parents & Caregivers Support Gathering
impactProjects.locationLabel: HIS AND HERS Care Family Hub
impactProjects.summary: A sensory-friendly afternoon empowering parents of autistic children with visual routine tools, calm regulation tips, and peer solidarity.
impactProjects.whatWasDone: Occupational therapists, parents, and community volunteers co-hosted an interactive sensory toolkit workshop while caring warmly for children in a calm adjoining playroom.
impactProjects.whyItMattered: Raising a neurodivergent child can feel isolating without practical community understanding. Sharing real tools restores confidence and joy.
impactProjects.whoItServed: Parents, guardians, siblings, and children on the autism spectrum.
impactProjects.whatGlowHopedToAchieve: To build a warm, stigma-free community where ASD families feel celebrated and supported.
impactProjects.documentedStory: Parents crafted custom picture schedules over tea while children explored wooden sensory puzzles in a gentle daylight room.
impactProjects.imageAlt: Parent and young autistic child playing calmly with colorful wooden blocks and picture cards

impactProjects.title: Safe Refuge & Rehabilitation Pathways Evening
impactProjects.locationLabel: HIS AND HERS Care Family Sanctuary
impactProjects.summary: An open-door evening combining gentle worship, confidential counselling, rehabilitation referrals, and safe-refuge guidance.
impactProjects.whatWasDone: We opened our gathering space for a calm evening featuring acoustic reflection, one-on-one counselling check-ins, and guided referrals to partner rehab and shelter facilities.
impactProjects.whyItMattered: Families battling trauma, addiction, or domestic danger need trustworthy bridges to nearby care facilities without shame.
impactProjects.whoItServed: Individuals, families seeking rehabilitation partners, and survivors rebuilding stability.
impactProjects.whatGlowHopedToAchieve: To bridge spiritual care, mental health listening, and practical safeguarding under one welcoming roof.
impactProjects.documentedStory: As evening settled over the sanctuary, attendees connected with counsellors, rehab liaisons, and prayer companions in warmth and dignity.
impactProjects.imageAlt: Sunlit restoration centre garden where counsellor and family member sit together
